summary: _(b) Pass any other orders, as this Commission deem fit and proper in light of the facts and circumstances of the instant case.”_ 5. CTUIL submitted that in the proceedings of Petition No.132/MP/2024, CTUIL had already pointed out that there are no enabling provisions in the GNA Regulations for allowing the request of the Petitioner and accordingly, vide Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 5.6.2024 therein, the Commission had asked CEA to convene a meeting with the participation of the Petitioner, CTUIL, GCIL, and other concerned stakeholders to resolve/propose the solutions to the concerns raised by GCIL/ WRLDC and the minutes of the said meeting incorporating the certain recommendations have already been placed on record of the said case. - 6.Considering the submissions made by the learned counsels for the Petitioner and CTUIL, the Petition was admitted, and Respondents were directed to file their reply. 8. The contentions of the parties were reiterated. In response to the specific query of the Commission regarding an agreement of TPL for sharing the dedicated transmission line and terminal bay, the learned senior counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the parties are yet to enter into a formal agreement. 10. During the course of the hearing the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that pursuant to the liberty granted by the Commission vide Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 6.2.2025, CTUIL has filed its reply wherein it has also placed on record the Minutes of Meeting held under the aegis of the Central Electricity Authority on 1.7.2024. It was submitted that the meeting was convened in terms of the direction issued by this Commission vide Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 5.6.2024 in Petition No. 132/MP/2024, which also involved a similar issue, and in the said meeting, a consensus was reached by all the stakeholders with respect to the manner in which metering, accounting, and scheduling were to be done, in a scenario where sharing of switchyard/terminal bays for connectivity to ISTS is required by injecting entities under Regulation 4.1 and drawee entities covered under Regulation 17.1(iii) of the GNA Regulations and the same may also be considered for the purpose of the present Petition. - 11.On a specific query of the Commission regarding agreement with TPL, learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that an in-principle agreement is there, and the parties are in the process of finalizing the Agreement. He further submitted that the representative of TPL is also present, and he will confirm it. - 13.Considering the submissions made by the parties, the Commission reserved the matter for Order. 22. We note that in Petition No. 132/MP/2024, the Commission vide RoP for the hearing dated 05.06.2024 in Petition No. 132/MP/2024 referred the matter to the CEA to convene a meeting with all stakeholders, including CTUIL, GRID-India, and the Petitioner to resolve/propose solutions to the concerns raised by GCIL/ WRLDC. The relevant portion of the ROP is extracted as under: “ _4. The representative of Respondent, GCIL, while pointing out their concerns to the proposal of the Petitioner, mainly submitted as under:_ _(h) The Petitioner has also placed reliance on the Commission’s order dated 29.1.2020 in Petition No. 299/MP/2018 in the matter of BALCO v. PGCIL & Ors. However, the said order may not strictly apply to the present case._ _5. Learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner vide its affidavit dated 4.6.2024 has already furnished its suggestions to the above concerns raised by WRLDC in its reply dated 17.5.2024, and Respondent, WRLDC / GCIL are yet to formally respond to these suggestions, in case they are not feasible as per them. Learned counsel also added that keeping in view that the proposal of the Petitioner is aimed towards optimal utilisation of the transmission infrastructure, the Commission may request CEA to hold a meeting with the participation of the Petitioner, CTUIL, GCIL, and other concerned stakeholders to resolve/propose solution to the concerns raised by GCIL/ WRLDC._ _7. Considering the submissions made by the learned senior counsel and learned counsels for the parties, the Commission ordered as under:_ _(a) Respondents to file their reply within 10 days with a copy to the Petitioner who may file its rejoinder, if any, within three days thereafter._ _(b) Respondent(s), WRLDC or GCIL, to file their response to the affidavit of the Petitioner dated 4.6.2024 within five days._ _(c) The CEA to convene a meeting with the participation of the Petitioner, CTUIL, GCIL, and other concerned stakeholders to resolve/propose solutions to the concerns raised by GCIL/ WRLDC and the Petitioner to file the outcome of the meeting before the next date of the hearing.”_
